chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his fathers, from 'Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The 'Aghlaf (one who is not fully proficient in recitation) does not lead the people in prayer, even if he is the best reciter among them, because he has neglected the greatest part of the Sunnah. His testimony is not accepted, and prayer is not performed over him (in congregation), unless he left that (leading or being led) out of fear for his life.
And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from 'Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Do not pray behind the Ghalī (exaggerator in religious matters), even if he agrees with you in opinion, and the unknown (one whose status is unclear), and the one who openly commits sin, even if he is moderate (in other matters).

key_terms.الْأَغْلَفُ: The one who is not fully proficient in Quranic recitation

ai.seo_question: Who is disqualified from leading congregational prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith establishes that 'Aghlaf' refers to one who neglects the Sunnah of recitation, a defect that invalidates his testimony and funeral prayer unless due to fear of harm. It further expands the criteria for valid leadership by excluding the Ghalī (exaggerator in religious matters), the unknown, and the openly sinful, emphasizing that theological or moral deviation disqualifies one from leading the congregation regardless of their other merits.
